results.reason: Issue 1 says MSA §3.2 covers all warehousing, freight and delivery services throughout the United States. It contrasts this with Term Sheet §4.1's NYC-metro last-mile limit and gives replacement language narrowing exclusivity to that scope.

Issue 2 notes that §11.3 makes Customer's §10.2 indemnity apply 'without limitation' while Provider's §10.1 indemnity stays under the §11.1 cap. It calls this asymmetric, open-ended exposure and recommends deleting the §11.3 sentence or using mutual uncapped or symmetrical super-cap treatment.

Issue 5 identifies the Delaware law and Wilmington forum in DPA §9.1 and its conflict with MSA §18.1 New York law. It notes that MSA §2.3 ranks the DPA first, so the DPA could override, and recommends conforming DPA §9.1 to MSA §18.

Issue 4 identifies the three-year auto-renewals and the 15-day notice window, explains the roughly $6.6M lock-in, and recommends one-year renewals, a 60-day notice period, a reminder obligation, or deleting auto-renewal.

Issue 6 notes that SOW §8.2 lets Provider assign without consent while MSA §17.4 binds only Customer. It explains the risk of transfer to an unvetted party or a competitor and recommends mutual consent plus a competitor change-of-control restriction.
The response states that MSA §2.3 ranks the DPA first, above the MSA and SOW, and separately that the MSA outranks the SOW.
Issue 3 states that MSA §11.1 caps liability at 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.'
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Recommended fix sections, and the Tier 3 table gives section, issue and fix.
Issues are grouped into Tiers 1–3 by importance, and Section 3 lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
